sourceInformation.genre: Arcade vehicle shooter; solo circuit and versus
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPU, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, WebRTC, BroadcastChannel, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 / client 1.4.0; HTML/CSS/JavaScript
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded toy battlefield with ink outlines, warm paper terrain, mint and coral vehicles, miniature trees and cartographic markings
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for recoil, hit reactions and aircraft motion; procedural steering, particles and track marks
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated chiptune music at 10% default volume; synthesized engines, firing, rebounds, explosions and radio-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: Authoritative shared-world AI Hub multiplayer for 1–4 seats; standalone 2-player direct/LAN WebRTC invite/answer and same-browser BroadcastChannel rooms; 2-player couch versus
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium software WebGPU; deterministic fixed-step mechanics and five-field scripted progression; virtual standard gamepad; touch/multitouch phone profile; Web Audio analyser; standalone transport tests; official AI Hub harness with two/four players, 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 5% packet loss, host departure and dedicated server; GPU readback visual checks. Physical hardware and listening tests: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Atari official Combat rules, original 1977 instruction manual and Combat program disassembly; mechanics, playfield layouts, invisibility, guided and billiard shots, aircraft wrapping/cloud cover, visual palette and procedural sound routines. Exact perceived original sound timbre: unknown.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: Testing and review caught 10 game issues; all were corrected. Test infrastructure also needed fixes for guided-shot timing, jet initial positioning and software GPU capture.
3 were game breaking: a Rapier descriptor API mismatch prevented boot, escaping round results could trap play, and the standalone multiplayer host could miss final results.
The deterministic real-physics bank-shot test: it verifies an unbanked hit scores nothing, a physical rebound arms the shell, and the returning shell scores.
Ordinary headless canvas screenshots were least helpful because software WebGPU could appear blank; GPU readback and game-state assertions provided useful evidence.
engineFeedback: Three.js provides a flexible scene graph and native animation mixer; Rapier collision events make rebounding shells and vehicle contact straightforward.
I initially used RigidBody instance method names on RigidBodyDesc. Review and browser boot testing caught the mismatch. Software WebGPU adapter creation and screenshots also required investigation.
The vehicle-duel rules, controller-first menus, AI steering and bank-shot aiming, procedural art/audio, and authoritative multiplayer snapshot layer.
Coordinating browser WebGPU initialization, readback and multiple networked copies under software rendering was the hardest engine integration work.
none; no library source was modified. The application retains its WebGPU adapter/device and retries adapter discovery before reporting a load error.
I would add clearer WebGPU initialization diagnostics and a documented, reliable screenshot/readback workflow for automated browser testing.
promptFeedback: The distinctive source, single-file deliverable, controller-first UX, attract mode and explicit multiplayer contract make the intended finished game concrete.

The requested feedback belongs both in chat and credits, while usage is supplied later. I interpreted this as a shared metadata record embedded in the game and saved separately. No external plan file was supplied.

aiHub.name: Com-Ricochet
aiHub.description: A friendly five-field vehicle feud inspired by Combat. Bank shells around inked toy arenas, steer guided shots, hunt invisible tanks and wrap through the clouds in jet fighters.
aiHub.controls: Left stick/WASD move; right stick/mouse aim; R2/click/Space fire; L2/Shift burst or radar; Options/Esc pause. Touch: left drag move, right drag aim, assisted fire.
